facts: The second-highest part in four-part music. Low voices of women (mezzo-soprano, contralto) and high voices of men (countertenor) sing it. A countertenor has a range from about E3 to D5 or E5
in_the_work_of_bach: Three arias of the corpus (measured): lowest note A3, highest note E5; the middle of the voice is A4; 90 percent of the time is between C-sharp 4 and D5
in_this_work: Range G3 to F5 in the orchestra file. Usual notes B3 to D5; E5 and F5 only at peaks

facts: The flute of the time of Bach has one key. Its lowest note is D4
in_the_work_of_bach: Flutes of the corpus (measured): from D4 to F-sharp 6; the middle is E5
in_this_work: Range D4 to G6. The players also have recorders
The flute players change to recorders for the most quiet numbers

facts: In A: the sound is a minor third below the written note. Its tone is "less assertive and more tranquil" than the tone of the oboe; its bell has the form of a pear
in_this_work: Each oboe player has an oboe d'amore

facts: In F: the sound is a fifth below the written note. A curved tube and a brass bell. Range from F3 to G5
in_the_work_of_bach: Movements 19, 48, 49, 59, 60, and 65. In movement 49 two of them are the only harmony. Corpus (measured): from F3 to E5
in_this_work: Each oboe player has an oboe da caccia. The audio uses the English horn

facts: The bass of the oboe group
in_the_work_of_bach: A part of the continuo group
in_this_work: One player: continuo, and solo lines in some numbers

facts: The baroque violin has a different neck, fingerboard, bridge, and bass bar, and gut strings
in_the_work_of_bach: Violins of the corpus (measured): from G3 to E-flat 6. The solo violin of "Erbarme dich": from B3 to E6
in_this_work: 4 first violins, 4 second violins, 3 violas. Highest note of the orchestra file: A6 for the violins

facts: A bowed instrument with frets. Most viols have six strings tuned in fourths with a third in the middle. The player holds it between the legs
in_the_work_of_bach: Movements 34, 35, 56, 57. Corpus, Trauerode (measured): from D2 to D5
in_this_work: One player. A solo voice in the number of the cross

facts: The word violone was used for different large bowed instruments, with three to six strings and sometimes with frets
in_the_work_of_bach: The bass line of the continuo. Corpus (measured): the continuo is between C2 and G4
in_this_work: 2 violoncellos and 1 violone. The violone sounds one octave below the written note

facts: A lute with a long neck and a second pegbox. The first two strings are tuned one octave lower. It played basso continuo in the baroque period
in_the_work_of_bach: The first version of the Passion has a lute. The Trauerode has two lutes
in_this_work: One player: chords and plucked bass notes. The audio uses the harp

facts: The chord instruments of the continuo play from a bass line with figures: the player makes the chords
in_the_work_of_bach: The organ is the usual chord instrument of the Passion. Most frequent figures of the corpus (measured): 6, 6 4, 6 5, 7 with a raised third, 5, 7
in_this_work: One organ (long chords) and one harpsichord (short chords, recitative)

facts: The orchestra of the Passion has woodwinds, strings, and continuo only
